## Two Changes to GPS Selective Availability

Selective Availability deliberately degraded public GPS signals for national security. The United States changed its use of the feature in May 2000, when, at President Bill Clinton’s direction, the government stopped using it to make civil and commercial GPS more useful worldwide.

A separate announcement followed in September 2007: the future GPS III generation would be procured without Selective Availability. This was not the operational switch that had occurred in 2000. It specified that the feature would be omitted from a future generation of GPS.
